<title level="1" right="Creature Family">[Elemental, Wood](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=345)</title>

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 204

At first glance, wood elementals might not seem to have the same destructive potential as their cousins from the [Planes of Fire](/Planes.aspx?ID=6), [Water](/Planes.aspx?ID=7), or [Air](/Planes.aspx?ID=4), but don't be fooled. The woods can be a dangerous place.

 Though some resemble animals, the elemental beasts presented here are still plants, and their life cycles reflect it. Vegetable lambs grow on rooted stalks, from which they can't be removed until they've matured (or perhaps ripened), leaving them dependent on their immediate surroundings for food. Moss sloths are little more than lumps of green fluff for the first century of their existence, only gaining limited mobility once they can grow their defensive wooden claws. 

<title level="2">Members</title>
[Carved Beast](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2675) (Creature 6), [Elemental Thicket](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2679) (Creature 11), [Living Grove](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2674) (Creature 5), [Moss Sloth](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2671) (Creature 2), [Nursery Crawler](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2672) (Creature 3), [Painted Stag](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2678) (Creature 9), [Pine Pangolin](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2676) (Creature 7), [Snapdrake](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2677) (Creature 8), [Twins of Rowan](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2680) (Creature 13), [Vegetable Lamb](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2669) (Creature 1), [Whipping Willow](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2673) (Creature 4)

<aside>
<title level="2" noclass="true" icon="/images/Icons/Sidebar_2_AdditionalLore.png">A Brain By Any Other Name</title>

Even if Lady [Shumunue](/Deities.aspx?ID=275) taught the wood elementals' ancestors to mimic animals, a wood elemental's consciousness is contained not in a brain but in its root system. Entities like [nursery crawlers](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2672), [living groves](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2674), and [carved beasts](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2675) use this to their advantage. That an elemental's wooden body can be carved and crafted, apparently without lasting harm, implies that they might not feel pain so long as their roots remain undamaged.
</aside>

<aside>
<title level="2" noclass="true" icon="/images/Icons/Sidebar_2_AdditionalLore.png">Wild But Unwild</title>

Many wood elementals are created by [kizidhar](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2681) and other powerful creatures on the [Plane of Wood](/Planes.aspx?ID=25) and placed in rote roles. Populating nature preserves and sprawling estates, they can be unsure how to behave if released into the wild. They're essentially born domesticated and will likely act far differently than the wild creatures they mimic, even in natural environments. Their natural predators are few, putting the elementals at less risk, although they're still sometimes eaten by giant termites or captured by some as pets.
</aside>

<title level="2" right="Creature Family Group">Elemental</title>
